checks.label: Angles are based on parts of a full turn, which is 360°: dragging the tip anywhere round the centre gives an angle from 0° up to but not including 360°, every quarter of the turn is reachable, and turning the arm on by a full 360° puts its tip back in the same place, so 30° and 390° are the same arm

The terminal side of the angle intersects the circle at the point (x, y), which is equivalent to (cos t, sin t): at whole angles all the way round, the arm's tip, measured off the drawing, lies on the circle, as far across as cos θ and as far up as sin θ, and the readout on each axis and the row under the picture give those same values

Sine is the ratio of the opposite side to the hypotenuse and cosine the ratio of the adjacent side to the hypotenuse: on the first screen the upright side opposite θ divided by the arm, the hypotenuse, both measured off the drawing, is what the up axis reads, the side along the across axis divided by the arm is what the across axis reads, and the arm is exactly as long as the circle's radius

Sine, cosine and tangent all have different positive or negative values depending on what quadrant they are in: at whole angles all the way round, a side of the triangle is drawn dashed exactly when the coordinate it stands for is negative, the readouts carry the same signs, the slope row's tangent is negative exactly where sine and cosine have different signs, and the signs written in each quadrant on the four-quadrant screen match the tip's signs there

Scientific calculators need to be used for trigonometry and should be in degrees mode: the calculator on the level-line screen is marked DEG at every height of the line, and its inverse sine gives the angle in degrees, the one an arm is drawn at, where radians would give a far smaller number

Other students incorrectly identified the x-coordinate as the sine ratio: the first puzzle offers the tip's across coordinate as a wrong answer, with its own hint and its own red working, and on every screen with readouts the sine sits on the up axis and the cosine on the across axis
cos² θ + sin² θ = 1 at every whole angle: the squares row always comes to 1, at 150° it reads 0.75 + 0.25 = 1, and on an axis one square is 0 and the other 1

tan θ = sin θ ÷ cos θ is the arm's slope, rise over run: at 150° the slope row reads 0.5 ÷ −0.866 = −0.577, at whole angles off the up axis it equals the drawn rise over run, and at 90° and 270°, where the run is 0, it says tan has no value

Two angles share each sine, mirror images across the up axis that add up to 180°: at every height of the level line from −1 to 1 each arm's tip lies on the circle and on the line, the calculator's angle lies between −90° and 90°, the row gives the second angle from it, at 0.5 the arms are at 30° and 150°, and at the very top and bottom the two arms are one

Each puzzle accepts only its right answer, every wrong answer has its own hint and its own red row of working, the answer appears once it is given, and before an answer nothing in the picture gives it away

No label sits on another label or a handle, or runs off the picture, on any screen in any state: puzzles answered right, wrong or with Why? open, the arm dragged all the way round, the level line at every height
